sources.title: City of Abbotsford — COR 004-2016, adopted remuneration history, 2011–2015
sources.locator: Attachment B, Report COR 004-2016 dated February 2, 2016, page 2 of 4; 2011–2015 remuneration table and following policy discussion
notes: The report lists the implemented remuneration separately for each year. The 2011 baseline began December 1; it is an annual rate, not the amount paid during that partial year.
The historical table records an increase in 2012, no change in 2013, and no increases implemented in 2014 or 2015. No amounts have been calculated from the accompanying CPI percentages.
The policy assigned one third of remuneration to an incidental-expense allowance. That share is already within the listed amount; benefits and separately reimbursed expenses are outside it.
The larger report package also contains later proposed rates. Those proposals are excluded from this history.

sources.title: City of Abbotsford — 2015 comparator market analysis
sources.locator: Attachment B, Report COR 004-2016 dated February 2, 2016, page 2 of 4, Table 2 — Comparator Market Analysis, 2015
notes: These are the report’s 2015 comparative office-pay figures, published in 2016. They are retained as survey observations, not as each comparator municipality’s adopted rate schedule.
The table prints whole dollars and does not provide a consistent breakdown of allowances, benefits or tax treatment. No gross-up or supplement has been inferred.
Abbotsford’s duplicate comparator row is omitted because its own adopted history is included separately.

sources.title: City of Prince George — Sainas council remuneration survey, September 2017
sources.locator: June 5, 2018 committee agenda, page 9 of 20; Sainas Consult report dated November 2, 2017, page 3, Council Member 2017 Salary
notes: The consultant surveyed municipalities directly and states that the data were current in September 2017. The report date is November 2, 2017; the hosting agenda is from 2018.
The salary table is separate from sections on acting-mayor pay, vehicle allowances, benefits and other allowances. Those components have not been added to the table amounts.

The report makes a blanket statement that one third of remuneration was tax free. Victoria’s own 2022 governance review says its remuneration had been fully taxable since 2009; the inconsistent tax statement is not used to convert or harmonize any amount.
Whole-dollar survey figures are preserved as reported, separately from municipal adopted schedules.

sources.title: City of Nanaimo — 2018 mayor and council compensation survey
sources.locator: Released 2019 Q4 meeting collection, printed page 149 (original attachment page 30), Attachment B — Mayor & Council Compensation Survey Results
notes: This is the 2018 survey attached to the December 17, 2018 remuneration report, preserved in the city’s released 2019 meeting collection. The survey vintage is 2018, not the collection’s 2019 year.

The Mayor and Councillor columns are transcribed separately from Estimated Acting Pay and Total. Survey estimates of acting pay rely partly on assumptions about time served and are described in row notes rather than added to the office-pay amount.
The historical tax-treatment column is retained in row notes. Proposed changes to compensate for the 2019 tax change and the comparator medians are excluded.
The survey prints whole dollars. Its Saanich figures are rounded compared with Saanich’s own rate schedule; both source editions may therefore appear.
Nanaimo’s $35,447 councillor figure differs from the $35,438 in its March 2016 news release. Both published figures are retained without silently substituting one for the other.

supportingSources.title: March 24, 2016 Nanaimo spending and amenities policy announcement

sources.title: City of Victoria — 2023 annual base salary survey, published February 2024
sources.locator: Drive Organizational Development report dated February 21, 2024, Table 1 on page 5; definitions on page 18
notes: The table is explicitly for 2023 annual base salaries. Its 2021 census and municipal-expense columns are context only and do not determine the salary year.
Amounts are published in thousands of dollars to one decimal place. Conversion to CAD preserves the published $100 precision; these are not exact dollar-and-cent payroll figures.
As a comparative survey, this source remains reported office pay even though it describes the surveyed amounts as base salaries. It is not a replacement for each municipality’s adopted rate schedule.

Allowances, benefits and acting-mayor arrangements are surveyed separately. This extraction includes Victoria and the eleven BC comparators; non-BC municipalities and statistical averages are excluded.

sources.title: City of Nanaimo — 2025 council remuneration survey, published February 2026
sources.locator: February 18, 2026 Finance and Audit Committee agenda, page 66 and Attachment C on page 123 — 2025 Council Remuneration Survey Results
notes: The report says staff surveyed comparable municipalities in summer 2025. These are the 2025 survey figures, not the report’s proposed or budgeted 2026 amounts.

Mayor and Councillor columns are separate from Acting Pay and Total. The table cautions that some acting-pay calculations assume a period of service; those figures are retained in notes rather than treated as fixed annual supplements.
The current Nanaimo row is retained exactly as printed in Attachment C. Later scenario tables use different prorated or budgeted amounts; no annual amount is back-calculated from those scenarios.
All values are reported in whole dollars. Review dates indicate review history, not necessarily rate commencement dates. The comparator medians and proposed 2026 increases are excluded.

sources.title: City of Nanaimo — 2003 indemnities documented in March 2005 council minutes
sources.locator: March 7, 2005 council minutes, pages 7–8, item 8(a), Current indemnity (2003) row
notes: The minutes explicitly label these amounts as the current 2003 indemnities and say remuneration had not been adjusted since fall 2003.
The following 2004 policy calculation and comparator-average alternatives are not treated as implemented rates. No intervening annual rows or later rates are inferred.

sources.title: City of North Vancouver — published 2022 annual remuneration rates
sources.locator: Mayor & Council page, Remuneration section labelled 2022 rates
notes: The page explicitly labels these as 2022 annual rates. They are not assigned to the year of retrieval or to the District of North Vancouver.
Acting-mayor pay is separately stated as $1,634 per month served and is not added to an annual councillor rate.

sources.title: City of Victoria — 2022 base remuneration in the governance review
sources.locator: July 2022 Governance Review, section 5.2.2 Current Practices, printed page 26
notes: The city-commissioned review expressly gives Victoria’s 2022 base remuneration and excludes external board/committee per diems, expenses and benefits.
The review says Victoria’s remuneration had been fully taxable since 2009. No tax adjustment is made here.

The comparative tables later in the report are not included. One table labels North Vancouver as the District while printing rates that match the City’s own 2022 page, and another flags an unverified older Kamloops rate.

sources.title: City of Victoria — adopted Council Remuneration Bylaw 24-075, 2024
sources.locator: Bylaw 24-075, sections 2, 6, 7 and 9; adoption block dated September 12, 2024
notes: The adopted bylaw specifies annual indemnities for 2024. It came into force September 12, 2024; its transition clause allows payment adjustments to deliver the full annual indemnity in that year.
The $1,750 additional councillor indemnity for acting-mayor duties before adoption is separate from the base. From November 1, 2024, the bylaw instead pays $1,750 for each month as acting mayor.
No 2025 or 2026 amounts are calculated from the CPI or future percentage formulas. The document used here includes the signed adoption block, not the earlier draft with blank adoption details.

sources.title: City of Abbotsford — January 2011 compensation review, explicit 2007–2011 rate interval
sources.locator: Tim Dillon & Associates, Compensation Review for Elected Officials, January 19, 2011, original report page 8 (PDF page 35 of the 2016 package), Table 6, January 1, 2007–November 30, 2011 historical row
notes: Table 6 explicitly gives annual base salaries of $86,600 for Mayor and $34,700 for Councillors for January 1, 2007 through November 30, 2011. The surrounding text identifies these as the existing rates implemented in January 2007.
The table’s other row recommends rates beginning December 1, 2011. Only its existing-rate row is extracted here; the later adopted December 2011 rates have a separate source entry.

The ten observations are calendar-year slices of one explicitly stated interval, not five independently observed annual payroll schedules. The 2011 slice ends November 30, and its amount remains the annual rate rather than a prorated payment.
The original report says its data are rounded. These amounts are displayed in whole hundreds and retain $100 source precision; no additional accuracy is inferred.

The report describes one third of Abbotsford’s base remuneration as tax free. That share is within the displayed base, not a supplement to add. Expense reimbursements, benefits and separately discussed allowances are excluded.
The source’s original Table 6 and its historical-row dates and amounts were checked visually on PDF page 35.
